coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 6–8 miles, Z2 (140–150 bpm range), rolling terrain if available but nothing steep. You're 5 days out from a 50K with 2,500m of vert; this is a shakeout, not a workout. Your resting HR is 56—down 8.7 bpm from your 30-day average—and your recovery score is 92/100, which means your body is primed. Don't waste that by going tempo. Keep it conversational, under 2 hours total, and finish feeling like you could do another easy hour. The goal is movement, not stimulus.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You've got 5 days to top off your glycogen stores without overloading your gut. Today and tomorrow, eat 6–8g carbs per kg bodyweight (aim for ~450–500g if you're ~75kg), distributed evenly across 4–5 meals. Lean protein (0.8–1.2g/kg) at each meal. Alpine 50Ks punish the unprepared stomach: salt intake now (3–5g daily), practice your race-day food once more in a training run this week if you haven't, and dial in your hydration baseline—aim for pale urine by Monday. Alcohol off, caffeine moderate after 2 PM.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your 8.3-hour sleep at 88.8% efficiency is exactly what you need in taper. Sleep is your performance drug here—don't compromise it for work emails. Target 8+ hours every night until Friday; go to bed 30 minutes earlier if you need to. Your HRV data isn't available, so use the resting HR (56) as your anchor: if it climbs back above 62, you're underdone on recovery. Ice baths are counterproductive this close to race day; focus on easy walking, foam rolling, and naps if possible during travel.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Five days is long enough to overthink and short enough that you can't fix anything. Lock in your race plan now—splits, aid-station nutrition, cutoff timings, where you'll push vs. survive—and stop tinkering. Your recent runs (12.27 mi and 8.31 mi, both at 128–129 bpm) show you're fit and running controlled. Slovenia's terrain is unforgiving but not technically harder than what you've trained on. Use these last five days to visualize the second half of the race when your legs are heavy, not to doubt the base you've built.
